# ztrevc

> Computes some or all of the right and/or left eigenvectors of a complex upper triangular matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ztrevc from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztrevc';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ztrevc(
    order,
    side, howmny,
    SELECT, strideSELECT,
    N,
    T, LDT,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `side` | `("left"\|"right"\|"both")` | in |  | one of `'both'`, `'left'`, `'right'` | specifies the operation type |
| `howmny` | `("all"\|"backtransform"\|"selected")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'backtransform'`, `'selected'` | specifies the operation type |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array` | in | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `T` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDT ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `T` |
| `VL` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × mm` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| ((side === 'left' \|\| side === 'both') && ldvl < N)` | leading dimension of `VL` |
| `VR` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × mm` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| ((side === 'right' \|\| side === 'both') && ldvr < N)` | leading dimension of `VR` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR actually used to store the eigenvectors |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | input array |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | output array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'R'`: compute right eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'L'`: compute left eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute both right and left eigenvectors.
- `howmny`:

  -   `= 'A'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors, backtransformed using the matrices supplied in `VR` and/or `VL`;
  -   `= 'S'`: compute selected right and/or left eigenvectors, as indicated by the logical array `SELECT`.
- `SELECT`: If `HOWMNY = 'S'`, `SELECT` specifies the eigenvectors to be computed. The eigenvector corresponding to the j-th eigenvalue is computed if `SELECT(j)` = .TRUE.. Not referenced if `HOWMNY = 'A'` or 'B'.
- `N`: The order of the matrix T. $N \ge 0$.
- `T`: The upper triangular matrix T. T is modified, but restored on exit.
- `VL`: On entry, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B' and `HOWMNY = 'B'`, `VL` must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the unitary matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by ZHSEQR). On exit, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', `VL` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix Y of left eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, Y$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the left eigenvectors of T specified by

  -   `SELECT`, stored consecutively in the columns
  -   of `VL`, in the same order as their
  -   eigenvalues.

  Not referenced if `SIDE = 'R'`.
- `VR`: On entry, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B' and `HOWMNY = 'B'`, `VR` must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the unitary matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by ZHSEQR). On exit, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', `VR` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix X of right eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, X$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the right eigenvectors of T specified by

  -   `SELECT`, stored consecutively in the columns
  -   of `VR`, in the same order as their
  -   eigenvalues.

  Not referenced if `SIDE = 'L'`.
- `mm`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR`. $\mathrm{MM} \ge M$.
- `M`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR` actually used to store the eigenvectors. If `HOWMNY = 'A'` or 'B', M is set to N. Each selected eigenvector occupies one column.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "both", "left", "right"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "backtransform", "selected"
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "left" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "left" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVL < max( 1, mm ) )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "right" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVR < N )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "right" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVR < max( 1, mm ) )`)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ztrevc.ndarray(
    side, howmny,
    SELECT, strideSELECT, offsetSELECT,
    N,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `side` | `("left"\|"right"\|"both")` | in |  | one of `'both'`, `'left'`, `'right'` | specifies the operation type |
| `howmny` | `("all"\|"backtransform"\|"selected")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'backtransform'`, `'selected'` | specifies the operation type |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array` | in | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `SELECT` |
| ↳ `offsetSELECT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `T` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `T` |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `T` |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `T` |
| `VL` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × mm` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `VL` |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `VL` |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `VL` |
| `VR` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × mm` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `VR` |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `VR` |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `VR` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR actually used to store the eigenvectors |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `RWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `RWORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'R'`: compute right eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'L'`: compute left eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute both right and left eigenvectors.
- `howmny`:

  -   `= 'A'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors, backtransformed using the matrices supplied in `VR` and/or `VL`;
  -   `= 'S'`: compute selected right and/or left eigenvectors, as indicated by the logical array `SELECT`.
- `SELECT`: If `HOWMNY = 'S'`, `SELECT` specifies the eigenvectors to be computed. The eigenvector corresponding to the j-th eigenvalue is computed if `SELECT(j)` = .TRUE.. Not referenced if `HOWMNY = 'A'` or 'B'.
- `N`: The order of the matrix T. $N \ge 0$.
- `T`: The upper triangular matrix T. T is modified, but restored on exit.
- `VL`: On entry, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B' and `HOWMNY = 'B'`, `VL` must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the unitary matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by ZHSEQR). On exit, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', `VL` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix Y of left eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, Y$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the left eigenvectors of T specified by

  -   `SELECT`, stored consecutively in the columns
  -   of `VL`, in the same order as their

  Not referenced if `SIDE = 'R'`.
- `VR`: On entry, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B' and `HOWMNY = 'B'`, `VR` must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the unitary matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by ZHSEQR). On exit, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', `VR` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix X of right eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, X$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the right eigenvectors of T specified by

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "both", "left", "right"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "backtransform", "selected"
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `RWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetRWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `ztrevc()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZTREVC`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/ztrevc.f).
-   The routine computes eigenvectors of a complex upper triangular matrix T obtained from the Schur decomposition. It can compute right eigenvectors, left eigenvectors, or both.
-   When `howmny` is `'backtransform'`, VL/VR should contain the Schur vectors on entry, and the routine back-transforms them to eigenvectors of the original matrix.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Uint8Array from '@stdlib/array/uint8/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import ztrevc from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztrevc';

// 3x3 upper triangular matrix T (column-major):
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );

const T = new Complex128Array([
	2,
	1,
	0,
	0,
	0,
	0,
	1,
	0.5,
	3,
	-1,
	0,
	0,
	0.5,
	-0.5,
	1,
	1,
	4,
	0.5
]);

const VR = new Complex128Array( 9 );
const VL = new Complex128Array( 9 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 6 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

// Compute both right and left eigenvectors:
const info = ztrevc( 'column-major', 'both', 'all', new Uint8Array( 3 ), 1, 3, T, 3, VL, 3, VR, 3, 3, m, WORK, RWORK );

const vrv = reinterpret( VR, 0 );
const vlv = reinterpret( VL, 0 );
console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'VR[0]:', vrv[ 0 ], vrv[ 1 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'VL[0]:', vlv[ 0 ], vlv[ 1 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZTREVC`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZTREVC computes some or all of the right and/or left eigenvectors of a complex upper triangular matrix T. Matrices of this type are produced by the Schur factorization of a complex general matrix: $A = Q \, T \, Q^H$, as computed by ZHSEQR.

The right eigenvector x and the left eigenvector y of T corresponding to an eigenvalue w are defined by:

$$
T \, x = w \, x, (y^H) \, T = w \, (y^H)
$$

where $y^H$ denotes the conjugate transpose of the vector y. The eigenvalues are not input to this routine, but are read directly from the diagonal of T.

This routine returns the matrices X and/or Y of right and left eigenvectors of T, or the products $Q \, X$ and/or $Q \, Y$, where Q is an input matrix. If Q is the unitary factor that reduces a matrix A to Schur form T, then $Q \, X$ and $Q \, Y$ are the matrices of right and left eigenvectors of A.

### Further Details

The algorithm used in this program is basically backward (forward) substitution, with scaling to make the the code robust against possible overflow.

Each eigenvector is normalized so that the element of largest magnitude has magnitude 1; here the magnitude of a complex number (x,y) is taken to be \|x\| + \|y\|.

</section>
